claim: During Drosophila embryonic nervous system development, neuroblasts express a programmed cascade of five temporal transcription factors.
source: During Drosophila embryonic nervous system development, neuroblasts express a programmed cascade of five temporal transcription factors that govern the identity of cells generated at different time-points.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about Drosophila neuroblast development, supported by the broader literature context.

claim: The five temporal transcription factors govern the identity of cells generated at different time-points.
source: During Drosophila embryonic nervous system development, neuroblasts express a programmed cascade of five temporal transcription factors that govern the identity of cells generated at different time-points.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the function of temporal transcription factors.

claim: The five temporal genes fall short of accounting for the many distinct cell types generated in large lineages.
source: However, these five temporal genes fall short of accounting for the many distinct cell types generated in large lineages.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the complexity of lineages versus the limited number of temporal genes.

claim: The late temporal gene castor sub-divides its large window in neuroblast 5–6 by simultaneously activating two cell fate determination cascades and a sub-temporal regulatory program.
source: Here, we find that the late temporal gene castor sub-divides its large window in neuroblast 5–6 by simultaneously activating two cell fate determination cascades and a sub-temporal regulatory program.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The sub-temporal program acts both upon itself and upon the determination cascades to diversify the castor window.
source: The sub-temporal program acts both upon itself and upon the determination cascades to diversify the castor window.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing regulatory interactions.

claim: The early temporal gene Kruppel acts as one of the sub-temporal genes within the late castor window.
source: Surprisingly, the early temporal gene Kruppel acts as one of the sub-temporal genes within the late castor window.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by expression and functional data.

claim: The temporal gene castor activates the two determination cascades and the sub-temporal program.
source: Intriguingly, while the temporal gene castor activates the two determination cascades and the sub-temporal program, spatial cues controlling cell fate in the latter part of the 5–6 lineage exclusively act upon the determination cascades.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data on castor function.

claim: Spatial cues controlling cell fate in the latter part of the 5–6 lineage exclusively act upon the determination cascades.
source: Intriguingly, while the temporal gene castor activates the two determination cascades and the sub-temporal program, spatial cues controlling cell fate in the latter part of the 5–6 lineage exclusively act upon the determination cascades.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data on spatial cue function.

claim: In the Drosophila embryonic CNS, neuroblasts sequentially express the transcription factors Hunchback > Kruppel > POU-homeodomain factors Nubbin and Pdm2 > Castor > Grainy head.
source: In the Drosophila embryonic central nervous system (CNS), neuroblasts (NBs) sequentially expresses the transcription factors, Hunchback (Hb) > Kruppel (Kr) > POU-homeodomain factors Nubbin and Pdm2 (Pdm) > Castor (Cas) > Grainy head (Grh) (Baumgardt et al., 2009; Brody and Odenwald, 2000; Isshiki et al., 2001; Novotny et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Temporal transcription factors temporally alter NB competence to determine the types of neurons and glia born at each step of lineage progression.
source: These factors temporally alter NB competence to determine the types of neurons and glia born at each step of lineage progression (Kohwi and Doe, 2013; Li et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The instructive capacity of five temporal genes falls short of explaining the diversity observed in Drosophila NB lineages.
source: However, because Drosophila NB lineages can generate an array of different cell types, the instructive capacity of five temporal genes falls short of explaining the diversity observed (Baumgardt et al., 2009; Tsuji et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Sub-temporal genes act in cascades downstream of the temporal genes.
source: Studies suggest that this regulatory challenge is solved by the activity of the so-called sub-temporal genes, which act in cascades downstream of the temporal genes, do not feedback on the temporal genes, and play a role in sub-dividing larger temporal competence windows (Baumgardt et al., 2009; Benito-Sipos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Sub-temporal genes do not feedback on the temporal genes.
source: Studies suggest that this regulatory challenge is solved by the activity of the so-called sub-temporal genes, which act in cascades downstream of the temporal genes, do not feedback on the temporal genes, and play a role in sub-dividing larger temporal competence windows (Baumgardt et al., 2009; Benito-Sipos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Sub-temporal genes play a role in sub-dividing larger temporal competence windows.
source: Studies suggest that this regulatory challenge is solved by the activity of the so-called sub-temporal genes, which act in cascades downstream of the temporal genes, do not feedback on the temporal genes, and play a role in sub-dividing larger temporal competence windows (Baumgardt et al., 2009; Benito-Sipos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Terminal selector genes activate repertoires of terminal cell fate genes such as neurotransmitters and ion channels.
source: Downstream of temporal cues, the specification of cell fate is subsequently controlled by determination genes, referred to as terminal selector genes, that activate repertoire(s) of terminal cell fate genes e.g., neurotransmitters and ion channels (Hobert, 2008; Wenick and Hobert, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Terminal selectors often act in combinatorial codes to dictate final and unique cell fate.
source: The terminal selectors have been found to often act in combinatorial codes to dictate final and unique cell fate (Allan and Thor, 2015; Baumgardt et al., 2007; Enriquez et al., 2015; Sharma et al., 1998; Thor et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Terminal selectors may act in cascades denoted coherent feedforward loops (FFLs).
source: In addition, terminal selectors may act in cascades denoted coherent feedforward loops (FFLs) (Mangan and Alon, 2003; Mangan et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: FFLs are common in E.coli and yeast gene regulatory networks.
source: FFLs are common in E.coli and yeast gene regulatory networks (Alon, 2007), but have also been identified in animals, including in both Drosophila and C.elegans (Baumgardt et al., 2009; Baumgardt et al., 2007; Etchberger et al., 2009; Johnston et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: FFLs have been identified in animals, including in both Drosophila and C.elegans.
source: FFLs are common in E.coli and yeast gene regulatory networks (Alon, 2007), but have also been identified in animals, including in both Drosophila and C.elegans (Baumgardt et al., 2009; Baumgardt et al., 2007; Etchberger et al., 2009; Johnston et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The Apterous neurons of the Drosophila ventral nerve cord constitute a group of interneurons expressing the LIM-HD factor Apterous.
source: The Apterous (Ap) neurons of the Drosophila ventral nerve cord (VNC) constitute a group of interneurons expressing the LIM-HD factor Apterous (Ap) (Lundgren et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Ap neurons can be subdivided into dorsal Ap neurons (dAp) and the Ap cluster.
source: Ap neurons can be subdivided into; (1) dorsal Ap neurons (dAp) that are a dorsal bi-lateral row of Ap neurons generated in abdominal and thoracic segments by NB4-3, and (2) the Ap cluster that are a bi-lateral group of four Ap neurons, denoted Tv1-Tv4, that are generated consecutively by NB5-6T in thoracic segments (Figure 1) (Baumgardt et al., 2007; Gabilondo et al., 2016; Park et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies and reference to Figure 1.

claim: Dorsal Ap neurons (dAp) are a dorsal bi-lateral row of Ap neurons generated in abdominal and thoracic segments by NB4-3.
source: Ap neurons can be subdivided into; (1) dorsal Ap neurons (dAp) that are a dorsal bi-lateral row of Ap neurons generated in abdominal and thoracic segments by NB4-3, and (2) the Ap cluster that are a bi-lateral group of four Ap neurons, denoted Tv1-Tv4, that are generated consecutively by NB5-6T in thoracic segments (Figure 1) (Baumgardt et al., 2007; Gabilondo et al., 2016; Park et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies and reference to Figure 1.

claim: The Ap cluster is a bi-lateral group of four Ap neurons, denoted Tv1-Tv4, that are generated consecutively by NB5-6T in thoracic segments.
source: Ap neurons can be subdivided into; (1) dorsal Ap neurons (dAp) that are a dorsal bi-lateral row of Ap neurons generated in abdominal and thoracic segments by NB4-3, and (2) the Ap cluster that are a bi-lateral group of four Ap neurons, denoted Tv1-Tv4, that are generated consecutively by NB5-6T in thoracic segments (Figure 1) (Baumgardt et al., 2007; Gabilondo et al., 2016; Park et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies and reference to Figure 1.

claim: Two out of four Ap cluster cells have a neuropeptidergic cell fate: the Tv1/Nplp1 and Tv4/FMRFa cells.
source: Two out of four Ap cluster cells have a neuropeptidergic cell fate; the Tv1/Nplp1 and Tv4/FMRFa cells (Baumgardt et al., 2007; Benveniste et al., 1998; Park et al., 2004), while Tv2 and Tv3 are Ap interneurons.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Tv2 and Tv3 are Ap interneurons.
source: Two out of four Ap cluster cells have a neuropeptidergic cell fate; the Tv1/Nplp1 and Tv4/FMRFa cells (Baumgardt et al., 2007; Benveniste et al., 1998; Park et al., 2004), while Tv2 and Tv3 are Ap interneurons.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: All four Ap cluster cells express Ap and the transcriptional co-factor Eyes absent (Eya).
source: All four cells express Ap and the transcriptional co-factor Eyes absent (Eya) (Miguel-Aliaga et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Two related terminal selector FFLs operate in Ap cluster cells to dictate Nplp1 or FMRFa cell fate: col>ap/eya>dimm>Nplp1 and ap/eya/dac>dimm/BMP>FMRFa.
source: Two related terminal selector FFLs operate in Ap cluster cells to dictate Nplp1 or FMRFa cell fate, col>ap/eya>dimm>Nplp1 and ap/eya/dac>dimm/BMP>FMRFa (Allan et al., 2005, 2003; Baumgardt et al., 2007; Miguel-Aliaga et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Each cell type-specific FFL cascade is triggered by specific temporal and spatial inputs established during lineage progression.
source: Each cell type-specific FFL cascade is triggered by specific temporal and spatial inputs established during lineage progression.
evidence: This is supported by the broader context of the study and previous work.

claim: The spatial input consists of the combinatorial action of the Hox homeotic gene Antennapedia (Antp), the Hox co-factors extradenticle (exd) and homothorax (hth), as well as the homeobox gene ladybird early (lbe).
source: The spatial input, conferred by body position, consists of the combinatorial action of the Hox homeotic gene Antennapedia (Antp), the Hox co-factors extradenticle (exd) and homothorax (hth), as well as the homeobox gene ladybird early (lbe) (Gabilondo et al., 2016; Karlsson et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The temporal input is mediated by Cas and Grh, the last two factors in the Hb>Kr>Pdm>Cas>Grh temporal cascade.
source: The temporal input is mediated by Cas and Grh; the last two factors in the Hb>Kr>Pdm>Cas>Grh temporal cascade (Baumgardt et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Spatial and temporal inputs activate the two terminal FFL cascades in all four Ap cluster neurons.
source: Initially, these spatial and temporal inputs activate the two terminal FFL cascades in all four Ap cluster neurons.
evidence: This is supported by the broader context of the study and previous work.

claim: Cas triggers several additional genes in the neuroblast NB5-6T that act to sub-divide the broader Cas window.
source: However, Cas triggers several additional genes in the neuroblast NB5-6T that act to sub-divide the broader Cas window.
evidence: This is supported by the broader context of the study and previous work.

claim: The sub-temporal genes consist of squeeze (sqz), nab and seven up (svp).
source: These genes were denoted sub-temporal genes, and consist of squeeze (sqz), nab and seven up (svp), which act to repress collier (col; Flybase knot) in the generic Tv2/3 neurons and the Tv4 cell (Baumgardt et al., 2009; Benito-Sipos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The sub-temporal genes sqz, nab and svp act to repress collier (col) in the generic Tv2/3 neurons and the Tv4 cell.
source: These genes were denoted sub-temporal genes, and consist of squeeze (sqz), nab and seven up (svp), which act to repress collier (col; Flybase knot) in the generic Tv2/3 neurons and the Tv4 cell (Baumgardt et al., 2009; Benito-Sipos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The repression of col in the Tv2/3 and Tv4 neurons prevents those cells from being specified into Tv1/Nplp1 neurons.
source: The repression of col in the Tv2/3 and Tv4 neurons prevents those cells from being specified into Tv1/Nplp1 neurons.
evidence: This is supported by the broader context of the study and previous work.

claim: Kr mutants show loss of Nplp1 expression in the dAp cells and in the Tv1 cells.
source: Whole VNCs of control and Kr mutants, at AFT, reveal loss of Nplp1 expression in the dAp cells, but also in the Tv1 cells.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1A-B.

claim: In Kr mutants, Eya is normally expressed in four cells of the Ap cluster.
source: In mutants, while Eya is normally expressed in four cells, Dimm and Nplp1 expression is lost in the Tv1 cell.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1C-D.

claim: In Kr mutants, Dimm and Nplp1 expression is lost in the Tv1 cell.
source: In mutants, while Eya is normally expressed in four cells, Dimm and Nplp1 expression is lost in the Tv1 cell.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1C-D.

claim: In Kr mutants, Dimm and FMRFa expression in the Tv4 cell is not affected.
source: Dimm and FMRFa expression in the Tv4 cell is not affected in Kr mutants compared to control.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1C-D.

claim: Nab and Col expression in the NB5-6T at St14 is similar in control and Kr mutants.
source: Nab and Col expression, in the NB5-6T at St14, is similar in control and Kr mutants.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1E-F.

claim: In Tv1 cells at St14, Col expression is similar in control and Kr mutants.
source: In Tv1 cells (dashed circles) at St14 (distinguishable from Tv2 cells by positive Eya but negative Nab expression) Col expression is similar in control and Kr mutants.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1G-H.

claim: At late St16, Col and Dimm expression is lost in the Tv1 cell in Kr mutants while Eya is un-affected.
source: At late St16, while Eya is un-affected, Col and Dimm expression is lost in the Tv1 cell in Kr mutants.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1I-J.

claim: In Kr mutants, Dac expression is observed in all four Ap cluster cells at AFT.
source: While Dac is usually expressed in three out of four cells in the Ap clusters at AFT, we find that in Kr mutants Dac expression is observed in all four Ap cluster cells.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1K-L.

claim: Dac is significantly upregulated in Kr mutants when compared to control.
source: Dac is significantly upregulated in Kr mutants when compared to control (***p<0.001, nctrl = 7 clusters, nKr = 10 clusters, Chi-square test).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of data shown in Figure 1M.

claim: Kr is not expressed in the NB5-6T at St14.
source: Kr is not expressed in the NB5-6T or (O) the Tv1 cell at St14.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1N.

claim: Kr is not expressed in the Tv1 cell at St14.
source: Kr is not expressed in the NB5-6T or (O) the Tv1 cell at St14.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1O.

claim: At St16, Kr expression commences in Tv1.
source: At St16, Kr expression commences in Tv1 (dashed circle), which is characterized by maintenance of strong Col expression.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1P.

claim: Kr expression in Tv1 is variably maintained into AFT.
source: Variably, Kr expression in Tv1 is maintained into AFT, identifiable by co-staining for Eya and Nplp1.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1Q.

claim: Kr shows two phases of expression in the NB5-6T lineage: an early phase and a postmitotic phase in the Tv1 neuron.
source: In summary, Kr shows two phases of expression in the NB5-6T lineage; an early phase, in line with its known role as an early temporal factor, and a postmitotic phase in the Tv1 neuron (Figure 1R).
evidence: This is a summary of experimental observations shown in Figure 1.

claim: Postmitotic misexpression of Kr in all four Ap neurons results in ectopic expression of Col, Dimm and Nplp1 in other Tv neurons.
source: Misexpression of Kr in all four postmitotic Ap neurons resulted in the ectopic expression of Col, Dimm and Nplp1 in other Tv neurons (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2A-D.

claim: The conversion of Ap cluster neurons to a Tv1 cell fate by Kr misexpression is accompanied by the loss of FMRFa expression.
source: The conversion of Ap cluster neurons to a Tv1 cell fate was accompanied by the loss of FMRFa expression (Figure 2E–H), but not by the loss of Dac or Nab expression (Figure 2I–L).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2E-H.

claim: Kr misexpression does not result in loss of Dac or Nab expression.
source: The conversion of Ap cluster neurons to a Tv1 cell fate was accompanied by the loss of FMRFa expression (Figure 2E–H), but not by the loss of Dac or Nab expression (Figure 2I–L).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2I-L.

claim: Kr rescue by UAS-Kr driven from elav-Gal4 restores Dimm and Nplp1 specifically to Tv1.
source: Kr rescue by UAS-Kr driven from elav-Gal4 restores Dimm and Nplp1 specifically to Tv1.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2M-O.

claim: Cross-rescue of Kr with UAS-col from elav-Gal4 rescues Kr mutants, evident by Dimm and Nplp1 expression in the Ap clusters.
source: Cross-rescue of Kr with UAS-col from elav-Gal4 rescues Kr mutants, evident by Dimm and Nplp1 expression in the Ap clusters.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2P.

claim: The role of Kr in the Tv1 neuron is to ensure the maintenance of Col, thereby ensuring the propagation of the col>ap/eya>dimm>Nplp1 feedforward cascade.
source: These results suggest that the role of Kr in the Tv1 neuron is not to act directly upon Nplp1, but rather to ensure the maintenance of Col, and thereby ensure the propagation of the col>ap/eya>dimm>Nplp1 feedforward cascade leading to Tv1/Nplp1 terminal differentiation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the rescue experiments and expression data.

claim: Kr expression in the Tv1 cell is not affected in ap, eya and col mutants.
source: To address this, we first analyzed Kr expression in ap, eya and col mutants, critical Tv1 cell fate determinants (Baumgardt et al., 2007), but did not observe any change in Kr expression in these mutant backgrounds (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Kr expression in the Tv1 cell is not affected in Antp and lbe mutants.
source: Analysis of Kr expression in the Tv1 cell in Antp and lbe mutants, using this marker combination, revealed that Kr is not affected in either mutant (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: cas mutants often display loss of Kr in the Tv1 cells.
source: We found that cas mutants often displayed loss of Kr in the Tv1 cells (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A-C.

claim: cas mutants show a reduction in the number of Kr-expressing cells in the entire NB5-6T lineage.
source: This was accompanied by a reduction in the number of Kr-expressing cells in the entire NB5-6T lineage (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Cas and Kr overlap extensively in the NB5-6T lineage in the wild type background.
source: The reduction of Kr expression in the entire NB5-6T lineage in cas mutants was mirrored by extensive overlap between Cas and Kr in the NB5-6T lineage in the wild type background (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Cas/Kr overlap is observed in a number of cells throughout the thoracic VNC.
source: Moreover, scanning the entire thoracic VNC we observed Cas/Kr overlap in a number of other cells (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: cas mutants show striking reduction in Kr expression throughout thoracic segments.
source: Analyzing cas mutants in the entire thoracic segments, we observed striking reduction in Kr expression throughout these segments (Figure 3G–H).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3G-H.

claim: Kr expression is not affected in grh mutants.
source: Finally, we analyzed Kr expression in mutants for the last gene in the temporal gene cascade; grainy head (grh), which is known to be expressed during the latter part of NB5-6T lineage development, and important for Tv4/FMRFa cell fate (Baumgardt et al., 2009). However, we did not observe any effect on Kr expression in grh mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Kr is activated in Tv1 by cas.
source: We conclude that Kr is activated in Tv1 by cas, and strikingly, that this regulatory connection extends into many late postmitotic cells in the VNC.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the cas mutant analysis and expression data.

claim: The regulatory connection between cas and Kr extends into many late postmitotic cells in the VNC.
source: We conclude that Kr is activated in Tv1 by cas, and strikingly, that this regulatory connection extends into many late postmitotic cells in the VNC.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the cas mutant analysis and expression data.

claim: Neither Antp nor lbe regulate Kr in the Tv1 neuron.
source: In contrast, neither Antp nor lbe regulate Kr in the Tv1 neuron.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the mutant analysis.

claim: Nab is not affected in Kr mutants or by Kr misexpression.
source: As described above, Nab is not affected in Kr mutants or by Kr misexpression (Figures 1E–H, 2K–L).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 1E-H and 2K-L.

claim: In both sqz and nab mutants, there is one extra Kr/Dimm expressing cell in the Ap cluster.
source: In contrast, in both sqz and nab mutants, we observed one extra Kr/Dimm expressing cell in the Ap cluster (Figure 4A–E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A-E.

claim: Misexpression of nab suppresses Col maintenance and results in loss of Dimm and Nplp1 from the Tv1 neuron.
source: Misexpression of nab suppresses the Col maintenance and results in loss of Dimm and Nplp1 from the Tv1 neuron (Baumgardt et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Kr expression is absent from the Ap cluster when nab is misexpressed from elav-Gal4.
source: In line with these findings, we addressed the effects of misexpressing nab in the Tv1 neuron, from elav-Gal4. We observed that Kr expression was absent from the Ap cluster in nab misexpression (Figure 4K–M).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4K-M.

claim: The sub-temporal genes sqz and nab act to restrict the expression of Kr to the Tv1 neuron.
source: We conclude that the sub-temporal genes sqz and nab act to restrict the expression of Kr to the Tv1 neuron, while, Kr does not reciprocally regulate the cas>sqz>nab feedforward loop.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the mutant and misexpression data.

claim: Kr does not reciprocally regulate the cas>sqz>nab feedforward loop.
source: We conclude that the sub-temporal genes sqz and nab act to restrict the expression of Kr to the Tv1 neuron, while, Kr does not reciprocally regulate the cas>sqz>nab feedforward loop.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the mutant and misexpression data.

claim: svp mutants display ectopic Col, Dimm and Nplp1 expression in the Ap cluster.
source: Previous studies found that svp mutants displayed ectopic Col, Dimm and Nplp1 expression in the Ap cluster, and that postmitotic misexpression of svp from ap-Gal4 could suppress expression of Col, Dimm and Nplp1 (Benito-Sipos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Postmitotic misexpression of svp from ap-Gal4 suppresses expression of Col, Dimm and Nplp1.
source: Previous studies found that svp mutants displayed ectopic Col, Dimm and Nplp1 expression in the Ap cluster, and that postmitotic misexpression of svp from ap-Gal4 could suppress expression of Col, Dimm and Nplp1 (Benito-Sipos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Svp is initially expressed by all four Ap cluster cells (St15-16), but is rapidly confined to Tv2 and Tv3, where it is maintained into AFT.
source: Svp is initially expressed by all four Ap cluster cells (St15-16), but is rapidly confined to Tv2 and Tv3, where it is maintained into AFT (Benito-Sipos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: In sqz and nab mutants at stage AFT, there is loss of svp expression in one cell and one extra Dimm expressing cell.
source: We find that in sqz and nab mutants, at stage AFT, there is loss of svp expression in one cell and also one extra Dimm expressing cell (Figure 4F–J).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4F-J.

claim: nab misexpression results in Svp expression in one extra cell coupled with loss of Dimm expression in one cell.
source: Conversely, nab misexpression results in Svp expression in one extra cell coupled with loss of Dimm expression in one cell (Figure 4N–Q).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4N-Q.

claim: sqz and nab control Ap cluster diversification by ensuring Svp expression in Tv2 and Tv3.
source: Hence, sqz and nab control Ap cluster diversification also by ensuring Svp expression in Tv2 and Tv3.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the mutant and misexpression data.

claim: In Kr mutants, Svp is expressed in one additional Ap cluster cell.
source: We found that in Kr mutants, Svp is expressed in one additional Ap cluster cell.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5A-E.

claim: Kr misexpression postmitotically in all four Ap neurons results in complete loss of Svp expression.
source: Conversely, Kr misexpression postmitotically in all four Ap neurons resulted in complete loss of Svp expression (Figure 5F–H).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5F-H.

claim: svp mutants show increased number of Kr expressing cells in the Ap cluster.
source: Analyzing svp mutants, we observed ectopic Kr expression within the Ap cluster (Figure 5I–K).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5I-K.

claim: Misexpression of svp from elav-Gal4 results in complete loss of Dimm expression from the Ap cluster but no loss of wildtype Kr expression in Tv1.
source: However, when we misexpressed svp from elav-Gal4, while we could reproduce the complete loss of Dimm expression from the Ap cluster, we found no loss of wildtype Kr expression in Tv1 (Figure 5L–O).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5L-O.

claim: svp, Kr double mutants show the typical extra expression of Dimm and Nplp1 observed in svp mutants.
source: Prompted by these findings, we analyzed svp, Kr double mutants. We found that double mutants showed the typical extra expression of Dimm and Nplp1 observed in svp mutants (Figure 5P–T).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5P-T.

claim: sqz-nab ensures maintained expression of Svp in Tv2/3 by repressing Kr.
source: These results demonstrate that sqz-nab ensures maintained expression of Svp in Tv2/3, by repressing Kr.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the mutant and misexpression data.

claim: svp acts as a potent repressor of col and dimm expression.
source: svp in turn acts as a potent repressor of col and dimm expression, and is necessary but not sufficient to repress Kr.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the mutant and misexpression data.

claim: svp is necessary but not sufficient to repress Kr.
source: svp in turn acts as a potent repressor of col and dimm expression, and is necessary but not sufficient to repress Kr.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the mutant and misexpression data.

claim: The key role Kr plays in the Tv1 cell is to suppress Svp expression, to safeguard the expression of col and dimm.
source: The key role Kr plays in the Tv1 cell is to suppress Svp expression, to safeguard the expression of col and dimm, and thereby ensure the propagation of the col>ap/eya>dimm>Nplp1 feedforward cascade leading to Tv1/Nplp1 terminal differentiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the mutant and misexpression data.

claim: Kr strongly suppresses Svp expression broadly in the VNC when misexpressed pan-neuronally using elav-Gal4.
source: To address this we misexpressed Kr pan-neuronally, using elav-Gal4. Intriguingly, we find that Kr strongly suppresses Svp expression broadly in the VNC (Figure 6A–B, E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6A-B, E.

claim: Combinatorial misexpression of col with lbe results in ectopic Ap and Svp expressing cells.
source: Indeed, co-misexpressing lbe and col together result in striking ectopic Ap and Eya expression (Figure 6C,L).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6C, L.

claim: Only a subset of ectopic Ap cluster cells generated by lbe and col co-misexpression express Dimm and Nplp1.
source: However, only a subset of these ectopic Ap cluster cells express Dimm and Nplp1, and are bona fide Tv1 neurons (Figure 6L).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6L.

claim: lbe and col are sufficient to activate an early 'generic' Ap cluster cell fate, with ectopic Ap and Eya.
source: This observation, together with previous studies (Baumgardt et al., 2009; Baumgardt et al., 2007; Gabilondo et al., 2016), indicate that while lbe and col are sufficient to activate an early 'generic' Ap cluster cell fate, with ectopic Ap and Eya, specification of the different Ap cluster cell fates i.e., Tv1/Nplp1, Tv2/3, Tv4/FMRFa requires several other inputs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the current data and previous studies.

claim: Specification of the different Ap cluster cell fates (Tv1/Nplp1, Tv2/3, Tv4/FMRFa) requires several other inputs beyond lbe and col.
source: This observation, together with previous studies (Baumgardt et al., 2009; Baumgardt et al., 2007; Gabilondo et al., 2016), indicate that while lbe and col are sufficient to activate an early 'generic' Ap cluster cell fate, with ectopic Ap and Eya, specification of the different Ap cluster cell fates i.e., Tv1/Nplp1, Tv2/3, Tv4/FMRFa requires several other inputs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the current data and previous studies.

claim: col and lbe co-misexpression triggers ectopic activation of Svp expression.
source: On this note, col and lbe co-misexpression also triggered ectopic activation of Svp expression, corroborating the idea that col and lbe act together to trigger a mixture of Ap cluster cell fates (Figure 6C,E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6C, E.

claim: Triple co-misexpression of Kr, lbe and col dramatically reduces the number of Svp expressing cells while still activating extensive ectopic Ap expression.
source: Indeed, while triple co-misexpression of Kr, lbe and col still activates extensive ectopic Ap expression, as anticipated, the number of Svp expressing cells is dramatically reduced (Figure 6D,E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6D, E.

claim: Adding Kr to lbe-col misexpression cocktail refines the effects and steers 'generic' Ap neurons exclusively towards the Tv1/Nplp1 cell fate.
source: Finally, adding Kr to this cocktail refines the lbe-col effects, and 'generic' Ap neurons are now exclusively steered towards the Tv1/Nplp1 cell fate, evident by a robust increase in the numbers of Dimm/Nplp1 cells (Figure 6M,N).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6M, N.

claim: lbe and col co-misexpression triggers extensive generation of ectopic Ap cluster cells, but due to simultaneous activation of Svp in many ectopic Ap cluster cells, a mixture of Ap cluster cell fates is generated.
source: We conclude that lbe and col co-misexpression, as anticipated, triggers extensive generation of ectopic Ap cluster cells. However, due to the simultaneous activation of Svp in many ectopic Ap cluster cells, a mixture of Ap cluster cell fates is generated.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the misexpression data.

claim: Adding Kr to lbe-col misexpression ensures robust suppression of Svp, thereby refining the effect of lbe-col into exclusively Tv1 cell fate.
source: Adding Kr to this misexpression cocktail ensures robust suppression of Svp, and thereby refines the effect of lbe-col into exclusively Tv1 cell fate.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the misexpression data.

claim: The temporal gene cascade results in the expression of Cas in the latter part of NB5-6T.
source: Combining the findings presented in this study with previous studies, we find that the temporal gene cascade results in the expression of Cas in the latter part of NB5-6T (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a summary combining current findings with previous studies.

claim: cas acts together with spatial input provided by Antp, hth, exd and lbe to activate col in the NB.
source: cas acts together with spatial input, provided by Antp, hth, exd and lbe to activate col in the NB.
evidence: This is a summary combining current findings with previous studies.

claim: col activates ap and eya in the early postmitotic cells, which represents a transient and generic Ap cluster cell fate.
source: col in turn activates ap and eya in the early postmitotic cells, which represents a transient and generic Ap cluster cell fate.
evidence: This is a summary combining current findings with previous studies.

claim: In addition to col, cas activates five other genes: grh, sqz, nab, svp and Kr.
source: However, in addition to col, cas activates five other genes, including the last temporal gene grh, and the sub-temporal genes sqz, nab, svp and, as shown in this study, Kr.
evidence: This is a summary combining current findings with previous studies.

claim: The five genes activated by cas (grh, sqz, nab, svp, Kr) engage in a postmitotic cross-regulatory interplay unique to each of the three cell types.
source: These five genes engage in a postmitotic cross-regulatory interplay, unique to each of the three cell types, which results in the propagation of the col>ap/eya>dimm>Nplp1 terminal selector cascade exclusively in Tv1, and the ap/eya/dac>dimm/BMP>FMRFa cascade in Tv4, while the Tv2/3 cells acquire a non-peptidergic interneuron identity.
evidence: This is a summary combining current findings with previous studies.

claim: cas activates Kr and svp, but restricted expression of sqz, nab and svp in Tv2-Tv4 (all of which suppress Kr) explains the confined expression pattern of Kr to Tv1.
source: cas activates Kr and svp, but how is Kr expression then restricted to only Tv1 and svp expression to Tv2/3? For Kr, restricted expression of sqz, nab and svp in Tv2-Tv4, all of which suppress Kr, can explain the confined expression pattern of Kr to Tv1.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data.

claim: The gradually restricted expression of svp in Tv2-3 is explained by Kr repressing svp in Tv1 and by grh repressing svp in Tv4.
source: The gradually restricted expression of svp in Tv2-3 is in turn explained by Kr repressing svp in Tv1, and by grh repressing svp in Tv4.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data.

claim: col activation requires additional spatial information provided by lbe, Antp, hth and exd.
source: Besides its activation by cas, col activation requires additional spatial information, provided by lbe, Antp, hth and exd (Gabilondo et al., 2016; Karlsson et al., 2010), which subsequently initializes the generic Ap cluster program, by activating ap and eya.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: cas alone activates grh and the sub-temporal factors.
source: In contrast, cas alone activates grh and the sub-temporal factors, which are then important for the cell diversification, whether by activating or repressing each other's actions, or the FFLs, or partake in the FFL (grh), in order to allocate the correct cell fate to the four Ap cluster neurons.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings.

claim: The four spatial inputs (lbe, Antp, hth and exd) act only on col, while the temporal input (cas) acts both on col and on the temporal and sub-temporal factors.
source: Remarkably, the four spatial inputs (lbe, Antp, hth and exd) act only on col, while the temporal input (cas) acts both on col, as well as the temporal and sub-temporal factors (sqz, nab, svp, Kr and grh).
evidence: This is a summary of the findings.

claim: Kr acts first early in the canonical temporal cascade and subsequently late in the sub-temporal cascade to ensure the specification of the Tv1 cell.
source: An unexpected finding in this study pertains to the dual role of Kr, first acting early in the canonical temporal cascade and subsequently late in the sub-temporal cascade, to ensure the specification of the Tv1 cell.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings.

claim: Dual expression of Kr, first in the neuroblast and subsequently in neurons, was previously observed in NB3-3.
source: Interestingly, dual expression of Kr, first in the neuroblast and subsequently in neurons, was previously observed in NB3-3, but the functional role of the second Kr expression pulse was not addressed (Tsuji et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: svp displays a dual expression and function, being expressed early in many NB lineages to suppress hb, then being re-expressed in several lineages.
source: svp itself also displays a dual expression and function, being expressed early in many NB lineages to suppress hb (Kanai et al., 2005), then being re-expressed in several linages, and in NB5-6T it acts to suppress col and dimm (Benito-Sipos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: grh is necessary and sufficient for FMRFa expression in Tv4 cells.
source: With regards to postmitotic activity, another example of a temporal gene acting postmitotically applies to the role of the last temporal gene, grh, which is necessary and sufficient for FMRFa expression in Tv4 cells, and can trigger ectopic FMRFa in Ap neurons when misexpressed postmitotically (Baumgardt et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: grh can trigger ectopic FMRFa in Ap neurons when misexpressed postmitotically.
source: With regards to postmitotic activity, another example of a temporal gene acting postmitotically applies to the role of the last temporal gene, grh, which is necessary and sufficient for FMRFa expression in Tv4 cells, and can trigger ectopic FMRFa in Ap neurons when misexpressed postmitotically (Baumgardt et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Temporal multi-tasking may be a common feature for many temporal genes, both in Drosophila and in higher organisms.
source: Hence, with several examples of dual (Kr and svp) and progenitor versus postmitotic roles of temporal genes (Kr and grh), it is tempting to speculate that this type of temporal multi-tasking may indeed be a common feature for many temporal genes, both in Drosophila and in higher organisms.
evidence: This is speculation based on the findings.
